But requirement material: Indian author, got promoted from associate to professor in 2022 at same university where UG/Grad. C1 supports Indian author/associate professor? The requirement is a conjunction. Substantive part: Indian author exists. But "got promoted..." unsupported. So partially_supported? The rules: partially_supported if claims establish at least one substantive material part. C1 does establish Indian author and associate professor. However the core requirement is promotion and same university. Is entity existence a material part? Yes maybe "There is an Indian author who..." C1 confirms author. But maybe the requirement is specifically promotion. It has multiple conditions. At least one substantive part: Indian author. But also "associate professor" yes. So partially_supported. Need cite C1 only.

R2: "They had pursued their PhD abroad at a Canadian university under the guidance of an Iranian professor." C2: Alka pursued PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada. Supports PhD abroad at Canadian university. Does not support under guidance of Iranian professor. So partially_supported with C2. Could C1? no. R2 material parts: PhD abroad at Canadian university; under guidance of Iranian professor. C2 establishes first. So partial.

R3: "who dreamt of becoming a writer but switched to mathematics at the end of high school and got their doctorate in Minnesota." This refers to Iranian professor. No claims mention Iranian professor, their dreams, switch, doctorate Minnesota. Unsupported. supported_by [].

R4: "The author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing their PhD." Does claim state "connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation"? It says exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. Vipassana maybe an ancient technique for liberation from outside knowledge, but not in claim. However C1 says book date 2016. C2 says pursued PhD but no completion date. Need 20 years after completing PhD. Not supported. It establishes author published a book connecting Mathematics and Vipassana (a technique? maybe from claim name but not ancient liberation). It doesn't establish 20 years after PhD. So partially_supported? There is substantial part: published book connecting mathematics to Vipassana. But "ancient technique for liberation" and timing not. If Vipassana not established as ancient technique for liberation by claims, maybe partial for book connecting math to Vipassana, author, title. But requirement specifically "book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing PhD". C1 supports book connecting math to Vipassana, but not ancient technique for liberation or timing. Partially.

R5: "then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book." No claims about journal article, title, similar topic, six years after book. Unsupported. supported_by [].

R6: "What is the title of that article?" This is question requirement? It asks title. Verified claims do not provide title. Unsupported. Could C1/C2? no. So unsupported.

That establishes Indian author? It doesn't explicitly say Indian. It says at University of Delhi, India. Is she Indian? Not necessarily. But likely "Indian author" from context? We cannot infer nationality from workplace. C1 statement: "Alka Marwaha is an associate professor ... at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India, and the author..." It doesn't state Indian nationality. The task requirement: "There is an Indian author who got promoted..." C1 does not say Indian. It says at university in India. Could that support Indian author? No, not nationality. It supports author and associate professor at India college. Is author at India college enough for "Indian author"? No. But material part: author exists, associate professor. But requirement specifically "Indian author" maybe unsupported. If we mark partial because author/associate professor. Is that a substantive material part? Yes the person is an author and associate professor. But the "Indian" part not established. The promotion not. So partial. But if strict, no part of promotion? However "associate professor" is part of promotion from associate to professor. C1 establishes current associate professor, but not promotion in 2022. So at least describes rank. I'd say partially_supported.

R2: C2 says Alka awarded scholarship to pursue PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada. "under guidance of Iranian professor" unsupported. Partial.

R4: C1 says book title and topic Vipassana and Mathematics, publication date. Does it connect mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation? Vipassana may be meditation technique, but claim doesn't say ancient or liberation. However the book title The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics. It supports book connecting mathematics and Vipassana. It doesn't support ancient technique for liberation or 20 years after PhD. Partial.

R5 unsupported. R6 unsupported.
